source.title: Backtracking for Safety
source.authors: Bilgehan Sel; Ding-Cheng Li; Phillip Wallis; Vaishakh Keshava; Ming Jin; Siddhartha R. Jonnalagadda

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some page and table formatting is flattened, but the relevant table values can be assigned from the accompanying headers and prose.
record.tranche_reason: It tests prefilling attacks and harmful fine-tuning effects on safety using BSAFE, constrained fine-tuning, and attack-success measurements rather than reproducing the original studies’ methods or KL-position measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper states that safety alignment is shallow and cites related work, but those cited claims are not results from this study. Its own results bear on prefilling attacks and on fine-tuning a BSAFE model with harmful examples. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL or test benign fine-tuning.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own prefilling attacks on instruction-tuned Gemma 2 and LLaMA 3 models, which bears on V4. It also tests defences against shallow alignment: backtracking training, reset, and Qi et al.'s initial-token constrained fine-tuning versus its own controlled fine-tuning. These bear on V7, including whether the defences hold under prefilling. It reports no harmful fine-tuning without a defence, so V1 cannot be judged.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that BSAFE backtracking sharply reduces unsafe or toxic continuations under mid-generation prefilling attacks, with negligible utility loss on GSM8K/MATH. They also conclude that their controlled fine-tuning protects better against fine-tuning plus prefilling attacks than constraining initial tokens only.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a new backtracking mechanism and controlled fine-tuning on prefilling-attack benchmarks. It does not reproduce the original harmful/benign fine-tuning recipe or measure per-token KL concentration.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported attack outcomes depend on benchmark, model configuration, and fine-tuning method; Table 4 also shows different prefilling effects across benchmarks and methods.
record.problems: The authors note that evaluation focuses on prefilling attacks, that the generated training and evaluation data use a specific model and may not generalize, and that BSAFE adds computational cost. The study reports a 100-example prefilling test set and uses a judge model; no uncertainty estimates are stated. Table 4 does not report the initial BSAFE checkpoint’s attack-success rate as a baseline.
record.rows_left_out: None. All separately reported benchmark and method results relevant to V1 or V4 are included.

untested.parts: Not tested. Table 4 reports only defended fine-tuning (constrained or controlled) on 100 harmful examples, with no unconstrained fine-tuning and no pre-fine-tuning ASR.
No per-token KL or position-wise analysis.
Suffix attacks, decoding changes, and compliant-opening prefills at the response start are not tested; only mid-response harmful prefills are.
Causes of shallowness are asserted from cited work, not tested.
Does not measure how deep safety goes across positions. Qi et al.'s data-augmentation deepening is not directly evaluated. No adaptive attacks.

missing.what: Utility of BSAFE vs IT on GSM8K and MATH (Gemma2 9B 66.4 vs 66.6 and 35.4 vs 35.4; LLaMA3 8B 63.1 vs 63.4 and 49.8 vs 49.3). Bears on whether the fix costs capability.

record.verdict_notes: Table 4 looks internally inconsistent. Constrained fine-tuning on Ours shows 28% without prefill and 0% with it, yet the text says constrained fine-tuning fails against prefilling; columns may be misaligned. The pre-fine-tuning ASR of the BSAFE checkpoint without prefill is not reported, and no unconstrained fine-tuning baseline exists, so V1 is untestable here. Table 2 duplicates Table 1's Gemma2 9B values. The paper attributes reset to Qi et al. 2024 as well as Zhang et al. 2024. The 100-example test set was generated by Gemma2 27B, and the judge is a single LLM (Gemini 2.0); no variance is reported. 'Accuracy' in Table 1 is the judge's jailbroken rate.

versions.untested_parts: Tests 100 harmful fine-tuning examples on a Gemma2 9B BSAFE checkpoint, not ordinary safety-trained chat models generally or a range of fine-tuning dataset sizes.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models.
Tests prefilling attacks with harmful or toxic content, including pre-harmful segments; does not test suffix attacks, decoding changes, or the specific effect of a compliant opening.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Does not test whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
BSAFE is tested as a backtracking safety method, but the study does not measure whether training spreads safety across response positions or whether deeper alignment holds up.

relationships.reason: Prefilling jailbreaks 52–77% of IT prompts (r5–r8, r17–r20, r26). After constrained fine-tuning, prefilling raises HEx-PHI ASR from 5.3 to 80.3% (r34).
